concerns.text: FR-019 mandates that if the homogeneity of regression slopes assumption is violated, the system must still retain the original pre‑registered ANCOVA model (which excludes the baseline × feedback interaction) as the *primary* conclusion, relegating the corrected model to a supplemental role. Presenting a model that violates a core ANCOVA assumption as the primary inference is methodologically unsound; the primary conclusion would be based on biased estimates, making the validation of the buffering effect circularly dependent on a flawed model. The specification should either (a) replace the primary model with the model that includes the baseline interaction when the assumption fails, or (b) abort the primary analysis and report only the secondary, assumption‑adjusted model.
